name: Spaghetti bolognese
notes: The weeknight workhorse. Simmer longer on weekends if you can.
method: Brown the mince in a big pot, then soften the onion, garlic and carrot in with it.
Stir in tomato paste, passata and the crumbled stock cube; simmer 20+ minutes (longer is better).
Cook the spaghetti, toss with a ladle of sauce, serve topped with the rest and parmesan.

name: Butter chicken (mild)
notes: Kid-mild — add chilli at the table for the grown-ups.
method: Soften the diced onion, then brown the chicken pieces.
Stir through the curry paste for a minute, add tomatoes and coconut cream, simmer 15-20 minutes.
Serve over basmati rice with naan; chilli at the table for the grown-ups.

name: Tacos
method: Brown the mince, add the seasoning and a splash of water, simmer 5 minutes.
Warm the shells; lay everything out in bowls.
Everyone builds their own — that's the point.

name: Fried rice
notes: Best with day-old rice. Clears out the vegetable drawer.
method: Scramble the eggs first and set aside; crisp the bacon in the same pan.
Add garlic, peas and corn, then the cold rice on high heat, tossing constantly.
Return the egg, season with soy and sesame oil, finish with spring onion.

name: Sausages, mash and gravy
notes: Steam some greens while the mash is going.
method: Boil the potatoes until tender; mash with butter and milk.
Grill or pan-fry the sausages, turning until browned through (about 15 minutes).
Make up the gravy, steam the greens, plate the lot.

name: Chicken stir-fry
notes: Sauce is 2:1:1 soy, oyster sauce, honey. Rice or noodles.
method: Mix soy, oyster sauce and honey for the sauce.
Stir-fry the chicken in batches on high heat; set aside.
Stir-fry the vegetables with garlic and ginger, return the chicken, add the sauce, toss with rice or noodles.

name: Homemade pizza night
notes: Friday tradition. Bases from the shop are fine — it's about the toppings.
method: Heat the oven as hot as it goes with trays inside.
Sauce the bases, let everyone build their own half.
Bake 10-15 minutes until the cheese blisters.

name: Oven fish and chips
notes: Crumbed fillets and oven chips — beach-night dinner without the queue.
method: Chips in a hot oven first — they need a 10-minute head start.
Add the crumbed fish for the last 20 minutes, turning once.
Microwave the peas, cut the lemon, done.

name: Lasagne
notes: Assemble in the afternoon, bake at six. Freezes brilliantly.
method: Make a quick bolognese: brown the mince, add onion, garlic and passata, simmer 15 minutes.
Layer sauce, sheets, ricotta and spinach; repeat, finishing with cheese on top.
Bake at 180°C for about 45 minutes; rest 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Chicken schnitzel and salad
notes: Shop schnitzels on busy nights; crumb your own on Sundays.
method: Pan-fry the schnitzels in a little oil, 3-4 minutes a side, until golden.
Toss the salad with dressing while they rest.
Serve with lemon wedges and rolls if it's been a big day.

name: Pumpkin soup
notes: Winter staple. Crusty bread is not optional.
method: Soften the onion and garlic, add the cubed pumpkin and stock.
Simmer 20-25 minutes until the pumpkin collapses, then blend smooth.
Stir through the cream; serve with buttered crusty bread.

name: Burrito bowls
notes: Taco night's healthier cousin — everything in a bowl over rice.
method: Cook the rice; brown the mince with the seasoning.
Warm the beans and corn.
Bowl up rice first, then everyone adds their own toppings.

name: Satay chicken skewers
notes: Grill or barbecue. Sauce: peanut butter, coconut milk, soy, lime.
method: Thread the chicken onto soaked skewers and grill or barbecue until charred and cooked.
Warm peanut butter, coconut milk, soy, lime and curry powder into a sauce.
Serve over rice with cucumber, sauce over the top.

name: Zucchini slice
method: Squeeze the grated zucchini dry; fry the bacon and onion.
Whisk eggs and oil, stir in everything else, pour into a lined slice tin.
Bake at 180°C for about 35 minutes until set and golden.
